# The Vesuvius Challenge Bible

> An edited, fully cited reference book (15 October 2026) on the carbonized Herculaneum papyri and the Vesuvius Challenge (2023 to 2026): history, papyrus and inks, X-ray imaging, every prize and winner, the scroll and fragment inventory, the digital unwrapping pipeline (segmentation, tracing, VC3D, ScrollFiesta, spiral fitting, flattening, rendering, ink detection), tools, data formats, community, compute and costs, open problems, how-tos, glossary, timeline, FAQ and bibliography.

Conventions: citations are [Key] links into the bibliography; unverified statements are in italics; no sentence claims a reading of any text that the cited sources do not report; numbers come from the cited sources or are marked as editors' arithmetic.

## Start here

- [index.md](index.md): chapter list with summaries and word counts
- [bible.md](bible.md): the whole book as one Markdown file

- [The Spiral Fit](md/19-spiral.md): The spiral fit is the main whole-scroll method in 2026. It models the scroll as an ideal Archimedean spiral deformed by a smooth, invertible map (a diffeomorphism), and fits that map to all available 
- [Flattening and Rendering](md/20-flatten.md): Flattening assigns each mesh point a 2D coordinate with as little distortion as possible; VC3D's production tool, flatboi, uses SLIM to minimize the symmetric Dirichlet energy. Rendering then samples 
- [Ink Detection](md/21-ink.md): Ink detection is "signal recovery, not reading": a model looks at a small patch of a surface volume and predicts, per pixel, the probability of ink. Labels began with fragments photographed in infrare
